data.name: NaziShoot
data.detailed_description:
Checkout And Wishlist Little Kingdoms


Acerca do jogo

In NaziShoot, you play as a soldier trapped behind enemy lines.Your objective is to kill Nazis and uncover their plans.

Conserve your ammo, get them plans, and most importantly, shoot nazis.

Features:

• FPS: NaziShoot is a first person shooter

• Classic Guns: Kar98, Mp40, Luger, Thompson, Panzerfaust and more

• Levels: Fight nazis in the city,beach and even at night

• Save/Load: You can save and load the game

• Nazi Plans: Your objective in each level

reviews.review:
Full disclosure: I received this game in a random prize drawing for free. Needless to say, no one making money from this game offered me any to review it.

[h1]Quintessential Steam Trash[/h1]

Oh my [i]word[/i], this game is terrible. "But Matt! You only played it for a few minutes!" someone might say. I have seen enough in this game to objectively declare it to be awful. Most of the time I was playing, my jaw was dropped at how bad this game is. It's not "so bad it's good," either. I load up to a menu with "Start, Load, Exit," and the title, playing some okay music. Honestly, I would say that the title music is the only good thing about this game. Everything else is positively awful. I could write paragraphs about how bad this game is, and ordinarily I would go to great lengths at explaining my feelings about a game, because most of the time, there are several positive qualities and aspects I have "middling" feelings on with the average decently made game.  NaziShoot is not "decently made" at all, though. The following is a list of negatives I observed in just a few brief minutes:

- Early 1940s Nazis are using Uzi SMGs as standard issue. Those guns didn't even exist in rare, early adopter form until the late 1940s well after the war was over.

- Jumping appears to make the player lift up one foot off the ground (~0.33 meters), and it is incredibly jerky.

- Anything 50+ feet away is incredibly gray and foggy. No, it's not a metaphor for "the fog of war." You cannot see things in the distance, and your enemies all spawn at a distance and can see you and shoot you, completely unaffected by this fog.

- As best I can tell, enemy gunfire instantly hits you and does not display muzzle flare at a distance, you cannot locate enemies that are invisible right in front of you if the gray foggy 50+ foot distance hides them from plain sight. even when they are shooting you. The only way I could find enemies was to deliberately stand around until I got shot, watching for the damage indicator to point at the Nazi, then I charged like an idiot at my enemy, taking him out.

- Killing Nazis is not of importance. The goal of each level seems to be reaching a blue glowing flowing thing which the game does not describe. You touch it, a loading screen comes up, then you're in the next level. You can just run right past Nazis if you don't take too many hits. I ignored two Nazis five feet away from the exit and just touched it, not caring about them.

- The game warns you to turn off the Steam overlay for the "best results," because the moment the Steam overlay displays anything, the screen gets a horrible white filter that makes seeing things even harder than before, as though the aggravating gray fog wasn't bad enough. This will not go away unless you completely close the game; exiting to the in-game menu and reloading your save is insufficient. One might argue that this is all okay because the game tells you to turn off the overlay. No. This is a game being sold on Steam, that was developed years after Steam's inception. If a game malfunctions when the Steam overlay comes up, that means the developer needs to fix the problem. This is absolutely unacceptable.

- Nazis casually walk against heavy objects like burned up cars, and the car will flip and roll around with the Nazi soldiers plodding along against the car, stuck behind it. In short, the physics and A.I. are atrocious.

- Music no longer exists after the main menu. The game is dead quiet except for sound effects. "Maybe the sound effects are great and it's realistic and immersive?" No. It's not. It feels like a video game with zero immersion and no gameplay draw whatsoever. Ammo floats around as giant, twirling clusters of bullets, and you can't pick up the enemy's Uzi SMGs. Like I said, no immersion. However, it's also too dull and quiet to feel like a video game in a good way, either.

- There is no real sensation of purpose or story in this game. You wander around, get shot at, and shoot back, and try to reach an exit. It is dumb and pointless, with virtually no redeeming qualities. This game looks like what someone who doesn't play video games thinks video games are like. Have you ever seen those cheesy fake video games on shows like NCIS when a PC game is relevant to the plot of the show? Well, those games look like they'd be a lot more fun than NaziShoot.

These were just the things I noticed in a tiny, tiny number of minutes with the game. Whomever wrote the title song did alright. Literally everything else in the game is just dreadful. NaziShoot, in the words of the otherwise forgettable villain on the Ant-Man film, "Your existence offends me." This game is the epitome of Steam trash/shovelware. I would not recommend it for a dollar, I would not recommend it for free, and I would not recommend playing it if someone offered to pay you minimum wage for doing so, unless you were starving to death, and that's just cruel...kinda like paying homeless people to have legitimate, violent "bum fights."
